text:
Sara: heads up — tenant 'clover-ai' opened a ticket: p95 inference latency jumped from 90ms -> 1.2s and started seeing 429s in eu-dedicated-pool-4 around 09:03UTC.
Kevin: noticed same during our infra sweep, saw repeated SM utilization spikes on host-3, temp sensors peaked ~85C. CPU fine.
Jordana: any autoscale events? did it fail to spin new slots?
Sara: autoscale logs show a scale-up request at 09:04 but scheduler didn't place new slice — kept retrying, eventual placement 09:12.
Marc: logs: ``scheduler: placement failed: insufficient MIG slot type a100-1g; attempted host-3 twice``
Lucas: ops-bot attached host telemetry: ``nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv`` output indicates temp bursts then fan ramp, then apparent thermal throttle flags in driver.
Kevin: could be a noisy sibling causing power/thermal saturation — not classic KV-cache lock. Also see MIG partition differences on host-3: two tenants on 1g slices, one on 2g.
Jordana: tenant reports also include increased error rate for small requests (low token count). That smells like tail latency amplification from cohost.
Sara: reproducing steps I ran: pinned a small perf test to eu-dedicated-pool-4 on same tenant; when co-located with a batch job from internal perf suite we get p95 jumps and 429s. When we evict the batch job, latency returns.
Marc: interesting — internal batch was GPU-accelerated decoding with long sequences, sustained SM/memory bandwidth. If thermal headroom is low, sibling can push neighbor into driver throttling, causing scheduler to delay response and rate limiter to kick.
Lucas: captured dmesg lines: "NVRM: GPU at risk of power throttling" around same timestamps.
Kevin: immediate mitigations: 1) migrate affected tenant off host-3 to another node (manual placement) 2) temporarily bump autoscale thresholds to allow more conservative placement 3) block background batch jobs from landing on dedicated pool nodes.
Jordana: can we add a placement rule to avoid hosts with temp>80C or recent thermal events?
Marc: we have telemetry but no hard placement rule — we can add a soft-avoid or cooldown window on thermal alerts. Quick patch: set scheduler preference for hosts without recent thermal alerts for 30m.
Sara: customer-facing update: "We're seeing co-located GPU thermal saturation on a host in your dedicated pool causing transient throttling and autoscale delays. We're migrating your workload and will follow up once placement stabilizes." :thumbsup:
Kevin: follow-up actions I logged in the incident ticket: ``- migrated clover-ai to host-9 at 09:15UTC; - flagged host-3 for batch eviction; - added 30m thermal-avoid soft preference; - infra ticket to add temp-based placement rule``
Lucas: adding snippet of the diagnostic command we used:
```
# check recent thermal events
kubectl logs host-monitor-pod --since=2h | grep "power throttl" -A3
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o DT
```
Marc: long term: consider stricter isolation for dedicated pools (disallow long-running high-memory bandwidth batch jobs) or enforce MIG partition uniformity so slices are comparable. Also consider KPIs: throttle_count per host -> trigger autoscale placement policy.
Jordana: any billing/customer impact? clover reported some failed requests; their SLA credits may apply if TL breached. Support team — advise on credits?
Sara: support will open billing review after we confirm incident window 09:03-09:20UTC. I'll add timeline to ticket.
Lucas: note for runbook: add step to check "thermal events" in host-monitor and prefer eviction over live-scheduling when thermal_count>1 in last 15m.
Kevin: closing loop: do we want a hotfix deploy to treat thermal-alert as immediate placement-avoid? or just soft-aversion now?
Marc: soft-aversion now (low-risk) and start dev on hard-avoid rule.
Sara: thanks everyone — marking this thread resolved after migration + host eviction. I'll post update in incident channel and notify clover. :white_check_mark:
